clue.text: Ferret round as down-and-out

blocks.note: a hob is a male ferret
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A ferret scurrying about like a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferret' looks like a verb meaning to rummage, but it is the animal, and a male ferret has its own name, HOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wanderer, which is what a down-and-out person is: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Means to rave over the Independent crossword's charms

indicators.note: to rave is to talk wildly and incoherently, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
this puzzle appears in the Independent, so its crossword is our crossword

explanation.surface: Solvers gush about how delightful the Independent's crossword is.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaks for the paper: the Independent crossword is OUR crossword. MEANS and OUR are mixed together to give ENAMOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to captivate them and make them fall in love, so it is a synonym of charms as a verb.

clue.text: Drugs crazy

blocks.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Drugs' supplies two of them, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackpot as an adjective describes eccentric, mad or wildly impractical ideas, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: I keep freaking out over large shape-shifting creature

indicators.note: someone freaking out loses all composure, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone keeps panicking about a huge monster that changes form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I keep' reads like the speaker's confession, but it is simply letters to be mixed with L.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish folklore a kelpie is a water spirit that takes the form of a horse or a human to lure travellers.

clue.text: Reject Macron's way - work with Spain and other countries

indicators.note: to reject is to send something back, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: the French president would call a street a rue
op is short for opus, a work
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A call to spurn the French president's approach and cooperate with Spain and its neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: Macron is the President of France, so his word for a way or street is French. Spain contributes its car-sticker letter before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain together with its neighbouring nations makes up the continent, so the definition describes the continent by membership.

clue.text: Sleazy place where rich man not getting head from Stormy

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter is taken
not getting something means going without it, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: The traditional name of the rich man in the parable of Lazarus
the opening letter of Stormy

explanation.surface: A seedy venue where a wealthy man fails to get favours from a woman named Stormy, a nod to a famous scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the Latin word for rich, used as the name of the rich man in Luke's parable; drop its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is an informal word for a disreputable bar or club, exactly a seedy establishment.

clue.text: One having unhappy experience hasn't departed

indicators.note: what something hasn't got is missing from it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a downer is a depressing experience
D is the timetable abbreviation for departed

explanation.surface: Someone going through a miserable time has not yet left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One having' reads as the start of a description of a sufferer, but it is the definition: a person who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is someone who has a thing, so a person who has property is its proprietor.

clue.text: Angelic youngster hugs the lady in charge

indicators.note: a hug wraps arms around someone, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout
the pronoun for a lady
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A sweet-faced child embraces the woman who is the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angelic youngster' looks like one phrase for a cherub, but the definition ends after 'Angelic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means like a cherub, the chubby winged infant of religious art, so it suits an innocent sweet-faced look.

clue.text: See lame teaching fooled believers in this

definitions.note: a description of the answer, not a synonym: the thing fooled believers believe in

indicators.note: something fooled has been tricked and messed about with, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letter C is spelt out as 'cee'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor teaching has duped people into believing in it, the jibe of a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter voices the sceptic's view in a puzzle full of Trump references. 'fooled' does double duty as signal and part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the answer from a denier's viewpoint: global warming is the thing that duped people are said to believe in.

clue.text: "Lettuce, me?" (Conservative great)

blocks.note: cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine
the third note of the sol-fa scale, sung as 'me' and also spelt mi
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A salad leaf asks if it is meant, and is told it is a fine Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the note between ray and fah, as in the Sound of Music song, and is spelt MI here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic is used informally for something enormous or of vast scale, as in a problem of cosmic proportions.

clue.text: One politician's a sex pest? Don't start, that's wrong

indicators.note: not starting means missing the opening, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a Member of Parliament
someone who gropes

explanation.surface: An accusation against a politician, cut short with a warning not to go there because it is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' sounds like a weary retort but tells you to drop the G of the sex pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper behaviour is unseemly or not right, so improper and wrong are near synonyms.

clue.text: Supreme Leader's content to live economically

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies within it, so only the inside letters are kept

blocks.note: to skimp is to live frugally; drop its outside letters

explanation.surface: The North Korean leader is happy to live frugally, a joke given his lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like an adjective meaning satisfied, but it is a noun for what is inside the word for living economically.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim Jong Un holds the title Supreme Leader of North Korea, as did his father and grandfather.

clue.text: Time to get behind this prolific peacemaker?

definitions.note: the question mark flags an ironic description

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A call that it is time to support a man who claims to end wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get behind' reads as 'support', but 'behind' is a noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump repeatedly claimed to have ended many wars and to deserve the Nobel Peace Prize; the question mark signals the irony.

clue.text: Even so, leaving first husband's hard

indicators.note: leaving first means being the earlier one to go, so the earlier of two matching letters departs

blocks.note: though can mean nevertheless
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: It is still difficult, losing a first husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you which H to remove: the earlier one of the two in the word for even so.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough and hard are synonyms in the sense of difficult, or of firm and resistant material.

clue.text: "All windmills evil" at first causing astonishment

indicators.note: at first points to the beginning of each word, so only opening letters count

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three quoted words

explanation.surface: A shocking claim that all wind turbines are wicked, the kind of thing Trump has said.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it a statement someone has made; Trump has often railed against wind farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is a feeling of wonder mixed with fear, close to the stunned surprise of astonishment.

clue.text: So monster is rebuffed

indicators.note: to rebuff is to send back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: an ogre is a man-eating giant

explanation.surface: So the monster gets snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' at the start looks like a casual opener but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to introduce a conclusion, just as so does.

clue.text: Runs into golf champion showing dignity in victory?

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A golf champion behaving well after winning, a dig at a famously bad loser and golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into the combined golf and champion pieces, between G and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is courteous good will, and being gracious in victory is the classic example of it; the question mark admits the definition by example.

clue.text: Stomach turned by Head of State's jerks

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards
the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the gut is the belly
the head of State is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A president's stomach is upset by some unpleasant people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like an insult for people, but it is a verb meaning pulls sharply. 'Head of State' reads as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug and to jerk both mean to pull suddenly and forcefully, so the plural verbs match.

clue.text: Ignoring Dead Sea's recurrent motif

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of account, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead
the familiar short name for the Mediterranean, with the article attached

explanation.surface: Passing over the Dead Sea, with its familiar pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead Sea' looks like a single place name, but it splits into a letter to drop and a sea to drop it from.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a recurring idea or melody in a work of art, the same as a repeated motif.

clue.text: Buried person with honour - noted criminal on guard

indicators.note: a criminal act is one that is wrong, so these letters are put out of order
a guard stands around what it protects, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
a Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: A decorated person who was once a notorious crook is laid to rest while watched over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted criminal' reads as a famous villain, but noted is the fodder and criminal tells you to rearrange it. The MBE is a British honour, below OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Entombed means placed in a tomb, a more formal word for buried.

clue.text: Again hiding one's prejudice

indicators.note: something hidden is covered over, so one piece is concealed within another

blocks.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music to mean repeat
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone concealing their partiality once more.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is the musical direction to repeat a passage, so it stands for again.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair inclination for or against something, which is what prejudice means.

clue.text: Doctor right - raised upsetting foot condition patient unable to fight

definitions.text: foot condition patient unable to fight
definitions.note: the whole phrase describes the condition that kept a patient out of the army

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down entry the letters run upwards

blocks.note: Bones is the nickname of the doctor in Star Trek, from sawbones, slang for a surgeon
R is the abbreviation for right
raised means up

explanation.surface: A doctor rules a patient unfit to serve because of a foot complaint, recalling Trump's Vietnam draft deferment.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump avoided the Vietnam draft with a diagnosis of bone spurs in his heels, which is why the patient cannot fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone spur is a small bony outgrowth, often on the heel, that can make walking or marching painful.

clue.text: One might be caught around centre

definitions.note: a description of the answer by what happens to it

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
a hub is the centre of a wheel or activity

explanation.surface: Something that might be caught near the middle, like a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' suggests cricket or a cold, but this is an angler's catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish popular with anglers, so it is one thing a fisherman might land.

clue.text: Dance top

blocks.note: first meaning: a Spanish dance in triple time
second meaning: a short open jacket

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance top' sounds like a garment for dancing; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lively Spanish dance and a short waist-length jacket worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Quiet Iranian leader once avoiding America

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: the Shah ruled Iran until 1979
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A discreet former ruler of Iran who stayed away from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' reads as an adjective describing the Shah, but it is the definition, an interjection.
explanation.definitionFit: Shh is the sound used to tell someone to be silent, the same as the command quiet.

clue.text: As was lost election, extremely suspect

definitions.note: the definition completes the sentence: as the lost election was, according to the loser

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept
something suspect is dodgy or not right, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of election

explanation.surface: A dubious claim about a defeat at the polls, Trump's line on 2020.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole clue as Trump would: his lost election, he says, was stolen. The wordplay mixes the lost letters with the ends of election.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply the answer after 'As was' and the sentence becomes the famous claim that the election was taken illegitimately.

clue.text: Guys are going for Nobel from the outset - one's perfect

definitions.note: the definition gives an example: perfect is one of them

indicators.note: the outset is the very beginning, so only the opening letter is taken
one thing going for another is swapped out in its favour

blocks.note: to guy someone is to mock or ridicule them
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
the outset of Nobel is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Men who think they deserve the Nobel prize from the start, each one flawless in his own eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' looks like a noun for men but is a verb meaning mocks. 'are' is the metric unit of area, 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is a grammatical tense, as in 'I have eaten', so it is one member of the set of verb forms.

clue.text: Back from Galapagos

indicators.note: taking something from a larger whole extracts a part of it, so the letters sit inside

blocks.note: inside the islands' name, near its end

explanation.surface: Returning from the Galapagos Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back from' invites you to read the letters reversed, but here the definition is 'Back' and the letters run forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago and back both refer to past time, as in two years ago or two years back.

clue.text: Leon and Marc cooked French rice

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients' form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two French-sounding men prepare a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: An obscure word; the two names are the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelcorn is emmer, an ancient wheat whose grains were also sold under the name French rice.

clue.text: Unusual team game? Could be

definitions.note: the definition is by example: game is one kind

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd sport for a group to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team game' looks like a sport, but game is wild animals eaten as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Game is the flesh of hunted animals such as venison or pheasant, an example of food from animals.

clue.text: Seat of government's ways of working - bully!

blocks.note: MOs, plural of MO, modus operandi
to cow someone is to intimidate them

explanation.surface: A cheer of 'bully!' for how a government operates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully!' looks like the old exclamation of approval, but it is a verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital of Russia, where the Kremlin and the government sit.

clue.text: Decapitated trunk? Not exactly

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, so the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: the torso is the trunk of the body

explanation.surface: A beheaded body, though the description is only approximate.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a trunk is already headless; removing its first letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so follows a figure to mean approximately, as in ten minutes or so, so it means roughly.

clue.text: Islanders' fees spent across bar

definitions.note: possessive noun for an adjective meaning of these islanders

indicators.note: spent money is scattered, so these letters are rearranged
lying across something spans it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Aero is a British chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Island people's charges paid at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but is a chocolate bar; Aero is a bubbly British chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Faeroese means belonging to the Faeroe Islands in the North Atlantic, so it describes things of those islanders.

clue.text: Petition over hiring queen for horseplay

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word runs backwards
to hire someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to sue is to petition a court
Qu is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A request about employing a queen for some rough fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseplay' looks like rowdy fun, but read it as a play about horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is Peter Shaffer's 1973 stage drama about a boy who blinds horses, literally a play about horses.
